title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from neighbouring pages): X is a differentiable (oriented or not) surface and x a point of X. Two objects are attached to x.
- S_x is the circle of tangent directions at x, i.e. the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up at x.
- D_x^* is the germ at x of the punctured neighbourhood.
Both have fundamental group canonically identified with T_x, a free Z-module of rank 1 (the local 'twist' or orientation lattice at x).

A_x is a family of 'angular' opens: arcs A of S_x, presumably small enough to be simply connected. Ep(A) is the corresponding sector germ in D_x^*.

For universal covers S̃_x → S_x and D̃_x^* → D_x^*, consider for each A:
- the T_x-torsor S̃_x(A) of sections of S̃_x over A;
- the T_x-torsor D̃_x^*(Ep(A)) of sections of D̃_x^* over the sector Ep(A).
H(A) is the T_x-torsor of isomorphisms between these two torsors. These are compatible with restriction for A ⊂ A'.

H(S̃_x, D̃_x^*) is the set of compatible families (h_A), i.e. global sections of this system. Definition: a 'correlation' between S̃_x and D̃_x^* is an element h of H(S̃_x, D̃_x^*). For fixed S̃_x and D̃_x^*, the correlations form a T_x-torsor.

Corr_x(X) is the groupoid of triples (S̃_x, D̃_x^*, h). The two forgetful functors to Revuniv(S_x) and Revuniv(D_x^*) are equivalences of categories (117). The previous page (111)-(116) supplies the abstract lemma that makes this independent of choices: given two equivalences of T-groupoids out of a common groupoid, the Isom-torsor functor is constant.

Modern meaning: a canonical, choice-free identification of the universal cover of the tangent circle with the universal cover of the punctured germ. This is the topological content of 'tangential base points': a direction at x (a point of S̃_x) determines a 'base point at x' for paths in X∖{x}. It is the formalism needed in La Longue Marche to define fundamental groupoids of surfaces with marked points or holes, based at boundary or tangential points, transported functorially along diffeomorphisms of germs (next page, (118)-(120)). This is in turn needed for gluing and for the Teichmüller tower and its Galois action.
errors: No mathematical error. Mild gap: the claim that the projections in (117) are equivalences tacitly uses that T_x acts compatibly on both sides (π1(S_x) ≅ π1(D_x^*) ≅ T_x canonically, via the deformation retraction / sector correspondence) and that H is nonempty. Nonemptiness holds since the system of sectors is cofinal and the arcs are connected; this is not spelled out.
The text writes 'Les corrélations entre S_x^* et D_x^{*~}'; this should be S̃_x and D̃_x^* (a slip in notation, or in the transcription).

ideas.what: Canonical correlation between the universal cover of the circle of tangent directions at x and the universal cover of the punctured germ at x, via compatible identifications of section-torsors over sectors
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / real oriented blow-up (boundary circle of the Kato–Nakayama-type blow-up); the 'local monodromy torsor'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points') for tangential base points; the real oriented blow-up is classical (A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama in the log setting)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981, circulated)

ideas.what: Groupoid Corr_x of correlated pairs, equivalent to each groupoid of universal covers; a T_x-torsor of correlations
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of torsor gerbes / trivialization of a T-torsor of comparisons

missed.claim: A careful, choice-free (transport-of-structure-compatible) construction of tangential base points on topological/differentiable surfaces, done in the Longue Marche manuscripts (c.1981), predating Deligne's 1989 tangential base points. The idea's presence in Grothendieck's work is broadly recognized, but this detailed formalism (correlations, the torsor H, the Corr_x equivalence) is unpublished.
missed.quote: On dit qu'on a une corrélation entre un rev. univ. S̃_x de S_x, et un autre D_x^{*~} de D_x^*, quand on s'est donné un élément de H(S̃_x, D̃_x^*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents the priority and the exact foundations Grothendieck used for base points 'at infinity' in the Teichmüller tower. It is mathematically standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: A rigorous but routine formalization of tangential base points (universal cover of the direction circle vs. the punctured germ). Historically interesting as an early (c.1981) careful treatment, but the idea is now standard and Grothendieck's use of such base points in the Longue Marche is known.
transcription_corrections: 'revient : à donnée d'un élément' → 'revient à la donnée d'un élément de H(A)'
'Les corrélations entre S_x^* et D_x^{*~}' → 'entre S̃_x et D̃_x^*'
'Cette identification est compatible avec les relations d'inclusion entre ouverts A⊂A'' — reads as compatibility with restriction maps for A ⊂ A' (the word 'ouverts' is uncertain)
'corrélés[?] de S_x et de D_x^*' — likely 'corrélés de S_x et de D_x^*', i.e. 'des triples ... de rev. univ. corrélés'
